Description: As a Kimi Code user, I want Maestro to delegate tasks to the `kimi` CLI so that I can use Kimi K3 as the model.
Acceptance Criteria: A `kimi-cli` runtime exists; it spawns the `kimi` CLI with the correct model flag and returns parsed output.

Description: As a Claude Code user, I want Maestro to delegate tasks to the `claude` CLI so that I can keep using Claude agents.
Acceptance Criteria: A `claude-cli` runtime exists; it passes `--model`, `--allowedTools`, and `--mcp-config` as appropriate.

Description: As a user, I want an API-only runtime so Maestro can run in CI, cloud, or with local OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Acceptance Criteria: The `openai-sdk` runtime implements a full tool loop and honors `allowed_tools`/`blocked_tools`.

Description: As a Claude user, I want an in-process SDK runtime that can intercept tool calls.
Acceptance Criteria: The `claude-sdk` runtime uses `claude-agent-sdk` and supports `can_use_tool` callbacks.

Description: As a Kimi user, I want the Agent Client Protocol runtime so Maestro can request permissions per tool call.
Acceptance Criteria: The `kimi-acp` runtime exists and wires ACP `request_permission` callbacks to tool guards.

Description: As a user, I want to add/override models in a YAML registry so Maestro can use new providers without code changes.
Acceptance Criteria: `~/.open-maestro/capabilities.yaml` and `.open-maestro/capabilities.yaml` are loaded and override defaults.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to match task requirements (reasoning, coding, vision, context) to model capabilities.
Acceptance Criteria: The router excludes models that cannot meet hard requirements and scores the rest by fit, cost, and latency.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to pick the cheapest capable model for each task.
Acceptance Criteria: `--cost-preference low` and inferred cost preference influence the selected model.

Description: As a user, I want `--prefer-local` to prefer Ollama/vLLM when available.
Acceptance Criteria: `--prefer-local` filters candidates to `provider: ollama`/`local` and probes `OLLAMA_HOST` automatically.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to refresh its static cost ranking periodically with live provider pricing.
Acceptance Criteria: A scheduled job (default weekly) fetches public price APIs and updates `relative_cost` values.

Description: As a user, I want the cheapest model to be skipped if it is more than 20%% slower than the fastest alternative.
Acceptance Criteria: Measured tokens-per-second from `latency.yaml` is used to enforce a configurable latency tolerance.

Summary: Markdown agent definitions with YAML frontmatter
Description: As an agent author, I want agents defined in Markdown so they are human-readable and version-controllable.
Acceptance Criteria: Agents load from `.md` files with `id`, `role`, `model`, `tools`, `skills`, and `required_capabilities`.

Description: As a user, I want project agents to override user agents, which override bundled agents.
Acceptance Criteria: `AgentLoader.load_tiered_dirs` resolves project → user → bundled precedence.

Description: As an agent author, I want agents to extend a base agent so I can avoid duplication.
Acceptance Criteria: The `extends` field merges scalar fields, tool lists, skills, and capabilities.

Description: As a user, I want to add skills at the project or user level so agents can use custom instructions.
Acceptance Criteria: Skills load from `./.open-maestro/skills/`, `~/.open-maestro/skills/`, and bundled `skills/`.

Description: As a team lead, I want Maestro to sync agents/skills from a Git repo so the team shares a single source of truth.
Acceptance Criteria: `maestro --add-agent-source`/`--add-skill-source` clones/updates Git repositories into `~/.open-maestro/sources/`.

Description: As a user, I want the MIT claude-mpm-skills repo available by default on first run.
Acceptance Criteria: The default `sources.yaml` includes `claude-mpm-skills` and syncs it automatically.

Description: As a user behind a firewall, I want bundled agents/skills to work without internet.
Acceptance Criteria: The wheel ships 15 bundled agents and 174 bundled skills; sync warnings are suppressed when offline.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to include the 47+ specialist agents from claude-mpm.
Acceptance Criteria: At least 30 additional specialist agents (frontend, backend, security, DevOps, QA) are bundled or sourced.

Description: As a user, I want each project to have its own persistent memory database.
Acceptance Criteria: `KuzuMemoryClient` binds to `cwd` and calls `kuzu-memory init` if no DB exists.

Description: As a user, I want semantic code search before delegation so agents get relevant code context.
Acceptance Criteria: `--search` recalls results from `mcp-vector-search` and includes them in the orchestration context.

Description: As a user, I want MCP servers to be discovered and passed to the correct runtime.
Acceptance Criteria: MCP config is loaded from project/user/env/flag; `claude-cli` gets `--mcp-config`, `openai-sdk` spawns stdio tools.

Description: As a user, I want to restrict which tools an agent can use.
Acceptance Criteria: `--allowed-tools`, `--block-tools`, agent `blocked_tools`, and SDK tool guards are enforced.

Description: As a user, I want a read-only mode that denies mutating tools.
Acceptance Criteria: `--permission-mode read-only` and `--deny-dangerous` are implemented across runtimes.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to warn me as context usage grows.
Acceptance Criteria: `ContextMonitor` tracks cumulative tokens and returns `warning`/`critical` at configured thresholds.

Description: As a user, I want a concise resume log when context pressure is critical.
Acceptance Criteria: `build_resume_log()` produces a markdown summary of progress, decisions, and next steps.

Description: As a user, I want to continue or branch a previous session.
Acceptance Criteria: `--resume` lists/reloads sessions; `--fork` copies a session under a new ID.

Description: As a user, I want to stay in one interactive session across multiple prompts.
Acceptance Criteria: `maestro --interactive` runs a `while True` loop until `/exit` or Ctrl-C.

Summary: Standard terminal line editing in interactive mode
Description: As a user, I want backspace and arrow keys to work normally in interactive mode.
Acceptance Criteria: readline is configured; reported issues with `^C` on backspace and `^[[A` on arrow keys remain.

Description: As a user, I want to know what step is running while I wait.
Acceptance Criteria: `ProgressIndicator` and event-bus handlers print `Thinking`, elapsed time, and step labels.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to infer `--reasoning`/`--fast` from plain English so I do not type flags.
Acceptance Criteria: `TaskProfiler.from_prompt` infers reasoning, coding strength, vision, and urgency from text.

Description: As a user, I want to inspect the execution plan before spending tokens.
Acceptance Criteria: `--show-plan` and `/plan`/`/dry` print selected runtime, model, and agent without calling the LLM.

Description: As a user, I want the PM to hand a task from a researcher to an engineer automatically.
Acceptance Criteria: `_run_with_handoff` exists but fails when the runtime does not support tool interception (e.g., `claude-cli`).

Summary: Artifact output routing to project folders
Description: As a user, I want generated docs to land in `docs/`, `requirements/`, `scripts/`, or `tests/`.
Acceptance Criteria: The orchestrator instructs agents to save outputs to conventional subfolders.

Description: As a user, I want to see which vendor and model produced each response.
Acceptance Criteria: Each turn prints `Vendor: ... / Model: ... / Runtime: ...` at the end of output.

Description: As a user, I want to type natural language tasks without memorizing CLI syntax.
Acceptance Criteria: Any non-slash input is treated as a task; flags and runtime are inferred automatically.

Description: As a user, I want milestone state stored in a project-scoped YAML file.
Acceptance Criteria: `MilestoneStore` reads/writes `.open-maestro/milestones.yaml` with Pydantic models.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to infer milestone status from existing project files.
Acceptance Criteria: `MilestoneDetector` scans artifact patterns (docs/blueprint*, tests/fixtures/, etc.) per milestone.

Description: As a user, I want `/milestones`, `/next`, `/complete`, `/blocker`, and `/track` commands.
Acceptance Criteria: All five slash commands are implemented and update local YAML state.

Description: As a user, I want agents to know the current milestone and exit criteria.
Acceptance Criteria: `format_prompt_context()` injects current milestone, completion, and exit criteria into prompts.

Description: As a user, I want to export a client-safe progress view.
Acceptance Criteria: `--export-dashboard json|markdown|html` writes the dashboard to stdout/file.

Description: As a user, I want to serve the dashboard from Maestro for local review.
Acceptance Criteria: `--serve-dashboard` runs an HTTP server on a configurable host/port.

Description: As a user, I want to publish the dashboard to `merven.ai` from the CLI.
Acceptance Criteria: `--publish-dashboard <url>` POSTs JSON with API key and project token.

Description: As a user, I want Maestro to pull the canonical milestone plan from Merven.
Acceptance Criteria: `--sync-milestones` fetches the plan from the Merven API and overwrites local YAML.

Summary: Dashboard styled with merven.ai design tokens
Description: As a user, I want the HTML dashboard to match the merven.ai brand.
Acceptance Criteria: HTML uses `#02040b` background, `#00bfaf` accent, Inter font, gradient cards.

Summary: Epic swimlanes with milestone Gantt charts
Description: As a user, I want epics as rows and their 8 milestones as Gantt bars.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard renders epic swimlanes with two rows of four milestones each.

Description: As a user, I want completed/in-progress/blocked badges to be readable.
Acceptance Criteria: Status badges and Gantt bars use high-contrast solid colors and text shadows.

Description: As a user, I want each Maestro project to have its own client dashboard.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard payload is keyed by project ID/token; Merven stores per-project dashboard state.

Description: As a team lead, I want a pre-built wheel to share with engineers.
Acceptance Criteria: `python -m build --wheel` produces `open_maestro-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl`.

Description: As a team lead, I want engineers to install Maestro with one command.
Acceptance Criteria: `scripts/install-ubuntu.sh` creates venv, installs wheel, and symlinks `maestro`.

Description: As a user on a firewalled machine, I want to install Maestro without internet.
Acceptance Criteria: Wheel + `pip install --no-index --find-links .` workflow documented and tested on WSL.

Summary: Bundle kuzu-memory and mcp-vector-search in install
Description: As a user, I want the install script to optionally install memory/search dependencies.
Acceptance Criteria: `install-ubuntu.sh` supports flags/env vars for optional extras.

Description: As a team lead, I want a guide for distributing Maestro to engineers.
Acceptance Criteria: `docs/DEPLOY.md` covers wheel distribution, install script, backends, MCP, troubleshooting.

Description: As a user, I want a documented way to wipe and reinstall the venv while keeping config.
Acceptance Criteria: `docs/DEPLOY.md` includes in-place upgrade and nuclear force-reinstall instructions.

Description: As a user, I want a live view of the current agent, runtime, model, and task state while Maestro runs.
Acceptance Criteria: `maestro --monitor` shows a Rich live panel with agent, runtime, model, task, context, and recent events.

Description: As a user or team lead, I want a running log of features released with each version.
Acceptance Criteria: `CHANGELOG.md` documents major/minor releases from 1.0.0 through 1.3.0.

Description: As a maintainer, I want Maestro source code in a remote GitHub repo so it is not only on one machine.
Acceptance Criteria: Repository created at https://github.com/mervenai/open-maestro with initial commit of v1.3.0.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the orchestrator to decompose my request into a sequence of agent steps so that complex tasks are handled by the right specialists in the right order.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a prompt like 'implement the budget import feature', when the planner runs, then it outputs a chain of 2-5 steps with explicit agent_id and purpose for each. Given a simple prompt like 'summarize this file', when the planner runs, then it returns a single-step chain. Given an unknown agent name returned by the LLM, when the chain is validated, then it is replaced with the closest matching registered agent or the default engineer.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the planned agent chain to run automatically without manual approval so that I can delegate complex workflows in one prompt.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a multi-step plan, when execution starts, then each agent runs only after the previous agent completes successfully. Given a step produces an error, when the chain executor detects it, then the chain stops and returns the error with a summary of completed steps. Given all steps complete, when the final step finishes, then the orchestrator returns a synthesized result containing outputs from every step.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the chain to be capped at 5 agents so that token cost and runtime stay bounded.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the planner returns more than 5 steps, when the chain is validated, then it is truncated to 5 steps with a warning logged. Given the chain reaches 5 completed steps, when the executor checks for dynamic expansion, then no additional agents are added.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want to see each agent's full output grouped under its name so that I can trace who did what.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a 3-agent chain completes, when the final response is rendered, then it contains clearly labeled sections like '## Researcher', '## Engineer', '## QA'. Given a single-step execution, when the result is returned, then it is formatted exactly as before with no extra grouping headers.

Description: As a Maestro operator, I want each agent in the chain to use the cheapest capable model available so that complex chains remain cost-effective.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a chain step requires deep reasoning, when the model is selected, then a reasoning-capable model is chosen using the existing select_runtime_for_task logic. Given two models satisfy a step's profile, when costs are compared, then the cheaper model is selected. Given a step requires tool use, when a local cheap model lacks tool support, then it is excluded even if it is cheapest.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want common workflows like 'implement a feature' to have predefined chains so that the LLM planner has reliable defaults and does not hallucinate.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a prompt classified as feature_implementation, when the planner runs, then it uses the predefined chain [research, engineer, qa] unless the LLM overrides with justification. Given a prompt classified as technical_analysis, when the planner runs, then it uses the predefined chain [research, documentation]. Given a prompt does not match any predefined pattern, when the planner runs, then it falls back to LLM-driven decomposition.

Description: As a Maestro user, I want the existing read-only to writer handoff to remain available so that simple writing tasks still work when chaining is disabled.
Acceptance Criteria: Given --chain is not passed and the selected agent is read-only, when the task requires writing, then the existing _run_with_handoff logic executes. Given --chain is passed, when the task can be decomposed, then the multi-agent chain executes instead of the 2-step handoff. Given --chain is passed but the planner returns a single step, when execution starts, then it behaves like a normal single-agent turn.

Description: As a Maestro user running with --monitor, I want the live monitor to show the current chain step and agent so that I can observe multi-agent progress in real time.
Acceptance Criteria: Given --monitor --chain is active, when a new step starts, then the monitor displays 'step 2/4: engineer'. Given a step completes, when the monitor refreshes, then the recent activity includes the completed step's agent name.

Description: As a Maestro interactive user, I want to toggle chaining mode with /chain so that I can enable or disable multi-agent behavior per session.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the user types /chain in interactive mode, when the command is processed, then chaining is toggled and the current state is printed. Given chaining is enabled, when the user submits a prompt, then the planner runs before agent execution. Given chaining is disabled, when the user submits a prompt, then the existing single-agent behavior runs.
